title: A less-cautious shield raise turns a terms-bound HOLD into a permanent one
body:
## Summary
raise_shield_for, given a verdict below a computed (terms-bound) HOLD, rewrites the row with shield_terms NULL, so the price HOLD becomes a 'raised' one that no reprice and no later CLEAR can clear.

## Description
crates/table-ledger/src/shield.rs:174-192: for a stored computed HOLD (terms set, not raised) and a raised ASK, the match falls to `Some(old) => (old, s.rule)` but write() is called with terms None. The deal now reads as a raised HOLD (Stored::raised, shield.rs:36), so the projection keeps it across a terms change and record_shield's raised branch (shield.rs:119-123) refuses every lower computed verdict. The second opinion only wanted 'at least ASK'; the owner instead gets a price_over_market HOLD on a price that is no longer the deal's. A correct fix needs the raised floor and the computed verdict stored apart (one verdict column today), i.e. a schema change, or a policy choice to drop one of them.

## Flow
- record_shield(HOLD, price_over_market, terms T) -> computed hold
- raise_shield(ASK) (second opinion) -> row rewritten HOLD/price_over_market, terms NULL
- reprice -> deal still held; record_shield(CLEAR, new terms) returns false
- control without the ASK raise: reprice drops the hold (shield None, not held)

## Expected impact
Owners whose second opinion returns ASK on a deal the price rule already held see a hold naming a price rule after the price changed and must release it by hand. A fix that keeps terms instead would lose the model's ASK floor on a terms change (policy-loosen).

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - a computed HOLD stays tied to its terms after a lower raise
Before: probe (temporary test, removed): after HOLD(T) + raise ASK + reprice: held=true, shield=HOLD, rule=price_over_market; CLEAR on new terms wrote=false, still held. Control (no raise): held=false, shield=None.
After: not built: either a second column for the raised floor (migration) or a policy choice which caution survives
Method: probe - temporary test in shield_tests.rs run and reverted; the gate rung needs the design choice first
Result: better
Gate: irreversible
evidence:
crates/table-ledger/src/shield.rs:174
crates/table-ledger/src/shield.rs:184-192 (write(.., None, ..))
crates/table-ledger/src/shield.rs:119-123
PROBE held=true shield=Some(Hold) rule=Some(PriceOverMarket)
PROBE after CLEAR wrote=false held=true
CONTROL held=false shield=None
instrument: shield_tests: record_shield HOLD(T) -> raise_shield ASK -> reprice -> assert the price hold no longer holds (only the raise's ASK floor) and record_shield CLEAR(T') writes

title: A MISMATCH or ended hold card says the offer lapses at the deadline
body:
## Summary
Hold cards for states with no deadline step (MISMATCH, and a shield hold on CAPTURED/RECEIPTED) fall through to 'the offer or order lapses at the deadline; no money moves', a lapse the state machine never performs.

## Description
crates/table-attention/src/lib.rs:182 makes MISMATCH (and any shield-held state) a Hold card; on_silence (lib.rs:231-247) has no branch for it, so it gets the default lapse line. transition(Mismatch, Deadline) is an error (crates/table-core/src/deal.rs:340-344), MISMATCH is terminal, and forecast() skips terminal states (crates/table-attention/src/forecast.rs:129), so word_silence never rewords it. The client maps the string at apps/desktop/client/src/lib/words.ts:403. Fixed: a hold-card line for a state with no deadline step that claims nothing happens at a deadline, plus its words.ts entry.

## Flow
- deal enters MISMATCH -> AttentionSource::item -> kind Hold
- on_silence default -> 'the offer or order lapses at the deadline; no money moves'
- Tumbler card: 'If you do nothing: the offer lapses at the deadline, no money moves'
- scheduler: Deadline on MISMATCH is an invalid transition; nothing lapses

## Expected impact
Owners looking at a mismatch or a held paid deal read a deadline outcome that never comes. Could break: the words.ts mirror if the Rust string changes without its entry.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - a hold card's 'if you do nothing' line names only what the state machine does
Before: walked: MISMATCH Hold -> lapse line, transition(Mismatch, Deadline)=Err; shield-held CAPTURED -> lapse line, pre_capture false; shield-held RECEIPTED -> same (3 of 3 claim a lapse that cannot happen)
After: 0 of 3 hold cards claim a deadline lapse for a state with no deadline step
Method: simulation - three states walked through lib.rs:182-247 and deal.rs transition(); the gate rung needs the new string and its words.ts entry (shared surface, outside this round's crate paths)
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: lib.rs test: for every DealState whose item is a Hold and where transition(state, Deadline/AutoVoid) is Err, on_silence must not say 'lapses'; plus the words.ts entry for the new line

title: open_rescue's 'live rescue' state list misses APPROVED and AUTHORIZED
body:
## Summary
The one-live-rescue-per-subscriber guard is a hand list of four states; a rescue deal the ledger lets reach APPROVED no longer blocks a second rescue for the same subscriber.

## Description
crates/table-ledger/src/rescue.rs:135 checks d.state IN ('PAIRING','AGREED','SETTLING','AWAITING_APPROVAL'). transition() accepts OrderApproved on any AWAITING_APPROVAL deal regardless of kind (crates/table-core/src/deal.rs:327), and SellerReceiptVerified admits APPROVED as a pre-receipt state (deal.rs:331). Fixed: derive 'live' from the state machine (not terminal and not yet paid) or refuse non-rescue events on rescue deals; either way a test over DealState::ALL.

## Flow
- open rescue for I-LIVE, send invoice -> AWAITING_APPROVAL
- apply_event(OrderApproved) -> APPROVED (accepted)
- open_rescue for I-LIVE next cycle -> Ok: two live rescues for one subscriber

## Expected impact
Only reachable if the runtime ever applies a buyer event to a rescue deal; then a subscriber could be sent two fix invoices. Could break: a stricter list refusing a legitimate re-open.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - at most one live rescue per subscriber whatever state the first is in
Before: probe (temporary test, removed): OrderApproved on rescue ok=true state=Approved; second rescue while first APPROVED ok=true
After: second rescue refused for every non-ended, non-paid state of the first
Method: probe - ledger-level only; runtime reachability not traced, and the live-set definition is a choice the worker makes against the instrument
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
crates/table-ledger/src/rescue.rs:135
crates/table-core/src/deal.rs:327
crates/table-core/src/deal.rs:331
PROBE OrderApproved on rescue: true state=Approved
PROBE second rescue while first APPROVED: ok=true
instrument: rescue_tests: for every state a rescue deal can reach by transition() from PAIRING, a second open_rescue for the same subscriber is refused unless the first is ended or paid

title: An unusable rescue-watch read leaves no outcome row in the audit chain
body:
## Summary
record_rescue_watch_read(None) only bumps the mutable tries/next_read_at columns; the chain shows the reserved rescue.watch_read and then nothing, so a run of failed PayPal reads is invisible afterwards.

## Description
crates/table-ledger/src/rescue_watch.rs:258-267: the None branch updates rescue_watches (a mutable row) and writes no audit row, while the Some branch writes rescue.watch_seen on a changed count (rescue_watch.rs:281-295). The tries counter is reset by the next good read (rescue_watch.rs:272), so after recovery no record says reads failed. Fixed: one rescue.watch_unread row (subscription_id, tries) per failed read, which needs entries in crates/table-ledger/src/audit_detail.rs ACTION_KEYS and crates/table-runtime/src/history/classify.rs (bookkeeping list) - both outside this context.

## Flow
- reserve_rescue_watch_read -> rescue.watch_read row
- PayPal read fails -> record_rescue_watch_read(None) -> tries+1, no row
- next good read -> tries=0; the failures are gone from every store

## Expected impact
The operator debugging a missed rescue sees reads reserved but no outcome. Adds one audit row per failed read (bounded by the day's read budget).

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - every reserved watch read has an outcome in the append-only chain
Before: 1 of 2 read outcomes (unusable) leaves no audit row; tries is reset by the next good read
After: 2 of 2 outcomes leave a row
Method: simulation - traced rescue_watch.rs:247-301; the gate needs the allowlist and history classify entries in other contexts
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: rescue_tests: record_rescue_watch_read(None) appends exactly one rescue.watch_unread row with no email and no 'dropped' key; audit_detail every_action test green

title: Pin the Tumbler's FORM_SIZE to the Rust form-size table
body:
## Summary
The client keeps a third copy of the seven window-form sizes; its test pins literals, not the Rust table that place() uses.

## Description
apps/desktop/client/src/windows/tumbler/logic.ts:21-27 hand-copies the sizes in crates/table-attention/src/placement.rs Form::size (now the single Rust table; FORMS is derived from it). apps/desktop/client/src/windows/tumbler/logic.test.ts:30 compares FORM_SIZE with literals. The house pattern is a vitest that reads the Rust file with comments stripped (apps/desktop/client/src/lib/mandateRules.test.ts:17).

## Flow
- read placement.rs, extract the Form::size arms
- assert FORM_SIZE equals them
- seed a drift in logic.ts -> red

## Expected impact
A size change in Rust would otherwise place the native window at one size and lay out the card at another. Test-only; nothing at runtime can break.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - one size table for the forms, checked from both sides
Before: 1 client copy (14 numbers) checked against literals, 0 against Rust
After: the client copy is checked against placement.rs
Method: simulation - the instrument is a client test outside this round's crate paths
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: vitest in apps/desktop/client/src/windows/tumbler/logic.test.ts reading crates/table-attention/src/placement.rs (comments stripped), comparing Form::size arms with FORM_SIZE; seeded drift goes red

title: Index audit_log by action for the market and watch day counters
body:
## Summary
Rejected: an audit_log(action) index does not meaningfully speed up the per-day counters in market_watch.rs and rescue_watch.rs.

## Description
checks_on (crates/table-ledger/src/market_watch.rs:26) and reads_on (crates/table-ledger/src/rescue_watch.rs:93) COUNT audit_log rows by action plus a CAST(at AS INTEGER) window; EXPLAIN shows SCAN audit_log. An index on (action, seq) turns it into SEARCH but the window filter is not indexable (at is TEXT under CAST), and the index is a migration.

## Flow
- 200k-row synthetic audit_log, 6 actions, python sqlite3
- time each counter query x20 before and after CREATE INDEX audit_by_action(action, seq)

## Expected impact
None; rejected.

## Evaluation
Claim: performance - faster daily allowance counts
Before: market.checked counter 22.44 ms, watch counter 18.17 ms (SCAN audit_log, 200k rows)
After: 22.04 ms and 14.35 ms (SEARCH via index): no gain on the market counter, a migration for 4 ms on the other
Method: experiment - synthetic store of the schema's shape run through the same queries on both arms
Result: not-better
Gate: irreversible
evidence: probe_audit.py: before q1 22.44 ms q2 18.17 ms (SCAN audit_log); after q1 22.04 ms q2 14.35 ms (SEARCH USING INDEX audit_by_action)
